paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His promises, and you get in by faith, not by earning it. Paul says the promise to Abraham came first, and the law came 430 years later, so the law could never cancel it (Galatians 3:17). The inheritance was never a paycheck. God "freely granted it to Abraham through a promise" (Galatians 3:18).

So what was the law for? Paul says it was added because of transgressions, and it became our guardian "to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith" (Galatians 3:19, 3:24). The law was never the finish line. It was pointing the whole time, like a sign on the road that says the bakery is ahead, and nobody camps out at the sign! Now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian (Galatians 3:25).

And here's why this matters to you. Paul says, "You are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus" (Galatians 3:26). God sent His Son to redeem those under the law so we might receive adoption, and He sent the Spirit into our hearts, crying out, "Abba, Father!" (Galatians 4:5-6). You are not hired help, baker. "You are no longer a slave, but a son; and since you are a son, you are also an heir through God" (Galatians 4:7).
